features.name: Ithaca Chasma
features.description: Ithaca Chasma is the great tectonic scar of Tethys: a trough system more than a thousand kilometres long that arcs across much of the icy moon. It may record a time when Tethys's interior froze, expanded, and split the outer shell like brittle rock.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: On a moon only about 1,062 km across, Ithaca Chasma is a truly global-scale fracture.

features.name: Ogygia Chasma
features.description: Ogygia Chasma is a shorter northern fracture that adds a second tectonic note to Tethys's battered surface. Its presence shows that the moon's crust did not simply break once around Ithaca Chasma; smaller fault systems also cut through the old ice.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Ogygia, the island home of Calypso in the Odyssey

features.name: Odysseus
features.description: Odysseus is one of the largest impact basins on any mid-sized icy moon. Its rim spans nearly two-fifths of Tethys's diameter, yet the basin has a softened, relaxed floor rather than the sharp relief expected from a fresh crater.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: An impact much larger than the Odysseus event might have shattered Tethys outright.

features.name: Scheria Montes
features.description: Scheria Montes rises inside the Odysseus basin, marking the rugged uplift left by the giant impact. This mountainous patch helps make Odysseus more than a simple circular stain: it preserves the rebound and collapse of Tethys's icy crust.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Scheria, island of the Phaeacians visited by Odysseus

features.name: Penelope
features.description: Penelope is the other major crater in the classic Cassini view of Tethys with Odysseus. Its broad rim and battered floor give a strong comparison point for reading impact ages across the anti-Saturn side of the moon.

features.name: Melanthius
features.description: Melanthius is a huge southern impact crater set in heavily cratered old terrain. Its subdued outline is a reminder that Tethys's water-ice crust can slowly relax large scars over geologic time.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Tethys is so ice-rich that big impact structures can sag and soften even in the deep cold.

features.name: Antinous
features.description: Antinous anchors another large southern crater field. Together with Melanthius and Telemus, it helps show how saturated the old terrain is: new impacts have repeatedly overlapped older scars.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Chief of Penelope's suitors in the Odyssey

features.name: Telemachus
features.description: Telemachus is a high-northern crater named for the son of Odysseus. It gives the fact sheet a useful polar-region anchor, away from the better-known Odysseus and Ithaca landmarks.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Tethys's named features draw heavily from people and places in Homer's Odyssey.

features.name: Eurycleia
features.description: Eurycleia sits in the northern cratered terrain, where smaller named craters help visitors read the surface beyond the giant basins. Its compact form contrasts with the broad relaxed floors of Odysseus and Penelope.

features.name: Polyphemus
features.description: Polyphemus is a mid-sized crater near Tethys's equatorial terrain. Its Odyssey name points back to the moon's naming theme, while its placement helps fill the map between the anti-Saturn crater basins and the tectonic chasmata.

features.name: E-ring Coated Leading Hemisphere
features.description: The leading side of Tethys is dusted by bright icy particles from Saturn's E ring, which is fed by material erupting from Enceladus. NASA's Cassini color maps show this hemisphere as lighter than the radiation-altered trailing side.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Neighboring Enceladus is literally painting Tethys with fresh icy dust.

features.name: Equatorial Pac-Man Band
features.description: Tethys has a bright equatorial band on its leading hemisphere, first noticed by Voyager and clarified by Cassini. The pattern is linked to high-energy electrons trapped in Saturn's magnetic field changing surface ice on a microscopic scale.

details.label: Texture cue
details.value: Bright equatorial band on the leading side

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Similar thermal patterns on Tethys and Mimas earned the nickname Pac-Man features.
